sources.entry: Litlyx - All-in-one Analytics Solution. Setup in 30 seconds. Display all your data on an AI-powered dashboard. Fully self-hostable and GDPR compliant. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Litlyx is a cookie-free, self-hostable web analytics tool with an AI-powered dashboard, positioned as an alternative to Google Analytics 4, Posthog and Mixpanel.
summary.what_it_does: Litlyx tracks website visitors by adding a script tag or installing the litlyx-js npm package and initializing it with a workspace ID. Once initialized, it automatically tracks page visits, real-time users and unique visitors. Developers can send custom events with optional metadata key-value pairs, such as a button click with product details. The README also shows sending a test event via a cURL POST request to an API endpoint. The dashboard can be self-hosted with Docker (via docker-compose after a prepare step) at localhost:3000, and self-hosted instances can receive data through script tag attributes for host, port and secure (HTTP/HTTPS). The README describes the project as GDPR compliant and cookie-free.
use_cases: track custom events on a website or app
monitor real-time users on a site
add analytics to a WordPress site
how_to_run: Open localhost:3000 to view the self-hosted dashboard
Point the tracking script's data-host, data-port and data-secure attributes at your instance
Alternatively, sign up at Litlyx.com for the hosted cloud and use your workspace_id
notable: Cookie-free tracking with no consent banner needed per the README
Install via a single script tag or the litlyx-js npm package
Custom events with arbitrary metadata fields
Self-hosting with Docker, with the full platform described as free
caveats: Scaling to more client seats requires one of the lifetime plans mentioned in the README
Self-hosting setup involves cloning the repo, a prepare step and Docker Compose
The README does not detail the AI dashboard features beyond the name
